summary: The main risk is request-scoped propagation: the repository currently stores registries, prompt builders, middleware, and active skills on shared bot instances. The design needs explicit tenant binding, request-local skill state, and a different prompt-layer strategy before the overlay itself is safe.

suggestions.title: Make tenant resolution a first-class request scope
suggestions.rationale: `RequestContext` is the existing ContextVar transport, but `UserContext` is only passed to `post_login()`/`clone_for_user()` and is never attached to it. `ask()` and `ask_stream()` accept tenant only through `**kwargs`, so it can leak into downstream LLM arguments unless consumed at the boundary. Add one resolver with the documented precedence, validate its result, and bind it around the entire ask/stream lifetime including tools and middleware.

suggestions.title: Enforce the HTTP tenant trust boundary centrally
suggestions.rationale: `ChatHandler` forwards request JSON through `data` and currently binds only `studio_scope`; custom method dispatch also merges all remaining body keys. `AgentHandler.ask_agent()` reads the body directly and calls `agent.ask()` without a resolved scope. A client-supplied `tenant` can therefore become the selected skill namespace unless both handlers remove it and pass only the server-resolved `RequestScope.tenant` through a trusted context.

suggestions.title: Do not store Telegram user tenants on a shared agent
suggestions.rationale: `TelegramAgentConfig` has no tenant field, `_build_permission_context()` hard-codes `tenant_id="default"`, `_build_user_context()` omits tenant metadata, and `_invoke_agent()` does not pass tenant. In singleton mode `post_login()` runs against the shared agent, so assigning each user's tenant to `self._tenant_id` would race. Add a static config tenant and pass it per request/context; keep instance defaults immutable.

suggestions.title: Replace the proposed per-tenant prompt-layer set
suggestions.rationale: `PromptBuilder` stores layers in a dictionary keyed by `name`, so multiple `available_skills` layers overwrite one another. Additionally, `condition` is evaluated during `configure()` and cleared by `partial_render()`, before the request tenant exists. Use one REQUEST-phase layer that renders from the current view, or add explicit variant support; tenant-varying prompt segments must not be provider-cacheable unless tenant identity is part of the cache key.

suggestions.title: Make active skills request-local before enabling singleton tenants
suggestions.rationale: The trigger middleware writes `bot._active_skill`, while `create_system_prompt()` mutates the shared prompt builder by adding/removing `skill_active`. Concurrent requests can therefore inject one tenant's skill into another request or clear another request's layer. Use a ContextVar or immutable per-request prompt composition; Telegram's direct `_active_skill` assignment must use the same mechanism.

suggestions.title: Inject a current-view resolver into every skill consumer
suggestions.rationale: `SkillFileToolkit` and `SkillRegistryToolkit` capture one registry during configuration, and trigger middleware captures one registry in its closure. Telegram listing and `/skill` resolution also read `_skill_file_registry` directly. A view implementation alone will not change these consumers; inject a resolver callback or a request-aware facade and remove direct global-registry reads from tools, middleware, narrative, and integrations.

suggestions.title: Define the overlay collision matrix and implement `global_only` explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `SkillDefinition` has no `global_only` field and `parse_skill_file()` ignores unknown frontmatter, so the accepted guard cannot work. Existing `SkillFileRegistry._register()` is first-wins only within one tree. The composed view must explicitly decide name collision, trigger collision with different names, and `global_only` behavior, then expose only the resulting effective indexes.

suggestions.title: Treat DB-backed skills as a separate overlay design problem
suggestions.rationale: `SkillRegistry.search_skills()` searches one FAISS index and `list_skills()` returns one namespace; selecting a tenant registry does not provide global fallback search. Define merge-before-limit semantics for search, preserve the source namespace with each result, and route `update_skill()` to that namespace. Also assess eager construction cost because each registry configures its own embedding/index state.

suggestions.title: Use secure path construction for tenant directories
suggestions.rationale: `validate_path_segment()` prevents traversal syntax but does not reject the reserved names, and tenant directory discovery would still follow an existing symlink. Build tenant paths through `secure_path()`, reject the complete reserved-name set before filesystem access, and validate the resolved tenant directory stays under the agent root. Keep the once-per-instance warning keyed only by validated tenant ids.

suggestions.title: Add concurrency and isolation tests before rollout
suggestions.rationale: The existing registry tests cover single-tree lookup and hot-add, while the integration tests exercise a mutable `_active_skill` and prompt builder sequentially. Add `asyncio.gather()` tests for two tenants on one singleton, exception/cancellation ContextVar reset, name/trigger/asset isolation, source precedence, absent-tenant warning deduplication, HTTP body tenant rejection, Telegram binding, and DB fallback/update routing.

suggestions.title: Specify prompt invalidation for learned global skills
suggestions.rationale: `save_learned_skill()` hot-adds to the live registry, but `render_skills_prompt_layer()` snapshots `list_skills()` at configure time. A learned global skill will be visible to tools and triggers yet absent from every static `<available_skills>` layer. Either invalidate/rebuild the request prompt index after a successful save or document that the prompt index is intentionally boot-time-only and test that contract.
